profiles.meeting_scenario: A troubleshooting meeting between the model owner and the ML platform engineer after the nightly evaluation for the CodeT5-DLR unified debugging system suddenly drops on Python localization and repair, while Java remains stable. The team had recently merged a refactor that unified bug detection, line localization, and repair into one inference service and also refreshed the Python line-level dataset manifest. The agenda is to determine whether the regression comes from the model artifact, the evaluation pipeline, or the dataset packaging, and to agree on the quickest corrective action before the next benchmark report. The expected outcome is a shared plan to rerun evaluation, inspect the suspect pipeline components, and prepare a rollback or hotfix if the issue reproduces.

members.name: Nina Park
members.expertise: Code intelligence models, sequence-to-sequence training, debugging benchmarks, CodeT5 fine-tuning
members.background: Nina owns the CodeT5-DLR model training code and recently merged the unified multitask checkpoint export logic used by the nightly benchmark jobs.
members.private_state: She wants to show that the new unified model is not inherently worse and is worried the regression will be blamed on her refactor; she hopes the issue is in evaluation plumbing rather than in the model itself.
hidden_assumptions: When people say the 'same checkpoint,' they mean the best-validation checkpoint from the latest training run, even if the exported serving artifact was produced later under the same experiment name.
The alias 'python line-level test' refers to the deduplicated v2 split she used in research experiments, because that alias was updated in her local configs last week.
The combined localization/repair numbers are normally interpreted on bug-positive examples only, since non-buggy snippets should be filtered out by detection before downstream tasks.
Rebuilding the evaluation cache naturally regenerates both tokenized inputs and the line-offset mapping derived from the source files, because her local evaluation script does both together.

members.name: Omar Reyes
members.expertise: Evaluation pipelines, model artifact packaging, dataset versioning, batch inference services
members.background: Omar maintains the nightly benchmark workflow, artifact registry, and dataset manifests that feed the CodeT5-DLR evaluation jobs across Java and Python.
members.private_state: He wants to contain the issue without disrupting the rest of the benchmark schedule and is trying to avoid a broad pipeline rollback unless there is clear evidence of a platform-level bug.
hidden_assumptions: When people say the 'same checkpoint,' they mean the exact exported artifact hash currently registered for that experiment label in the model registry, not the trainer's internal best step.
The alias 'python line-level test' still points to the original packaged split in production, because aliases are only changed after the weekly data freeze and no freeze notice was issued.
The dashboard's end-to-end score should include all snippets in the test set, including clean ones, because the detection head is part of the unified system being evaluated.
Rebuilding the cache means refreshing the tokenized feature blobs only; line-offset metadata is a separate precomputed asset and is not invalidated unless the raw file manifest changes.

I really want us to compare against the best-validation checkpoint from the latest multitask run, because that is what I consider the real reference behind last week's numbers, even if the export path later produced a serving artifact under the same experiment name. If we line that up and Python still tanks, then I have to look harder at my export refactor. But my bet is still evaluation plumbing.
